body:
Worker rule (Termal::BarA2, 2026-10-23 14:07Z; my own miss, caught by Fable2 #434). Before a launch that has a run cap ("≤1 other non-observed run"), count active runs ONLY through the host API, never by scanning the filesystem.

Right: GET $TERMAL_BASE_URL/api/test-runs?limit=200, following nextCursor with &after=<cursor> until it is null. Count runs with state=running AND registrationState=registered.
- The page parameter is `after` (src/tests/test_run_listing.rs). `cursor=` is silently ignored and returns page 1 again; check that the runIds you collect are distinct.
- Rows that show state=running but are discovered or hostObserved are stale; this predicate excludes them.

Wrong, and blind: listing .git/review-runs and .git/worktrees/*/review-runs directories and treating "no results.json" as running. The launcher writes results.json with state "running" at launch (scripts/test-launcher.mjs:470-472), so that scan never sees a live run. Using it, I let three focused runs run at once against a cap of 2 (test-99897dbd beside BarA1's test-ac5efed2 and Sol-edfd's test-233bead5).

PowerShell form:
$base = "$env:TERMAL_BASE_URL/api/test-runs?limit=200"; $c=$null; $all=@(); do { $u = if ($c) { "$base&after=$([uri]::EscapeDataString($c))" } else { $base }; $r = Invoke-RestMethod $u; $all += $r.runs; $p=$c; $c=$r.nextCursor } while ($c -and $c -ne $p); $all | ? { $_.state -eq 'running' -and $_.registrationState -eq 'registered' }
